source.title: When Waiting is not an Option: Learning Options with a Deliberation Cost
source.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-18)

confidence_rationale: Directly documents the specific failure shape ARC-130 warns about: within the option-critic framework (see companion 2017 entry in this directory), options that formally exist, are represented, and are locally operable nonetheless collapse into degenerate solutions absent an explicit regularizer -- either terminating on almost every step (never accumulating committed, multi-step behaviour) or running for an entire episode regardless of state (never exhibiting state-sensitive competitive authority). This is an external, non-REE, empirically-documented instance of ARC-130's central claim that 'authority at one internal selection boundary does not by itself establish that authority reaches committed behaviour' -- here, the option is selected and begins executing (an internal selection event) but the architecture-as-trained does not reliably carry that selection through to a stable, temporally-extended, ecologically meaningful commitment without an additional cost term designed specifically to make that gap visible and correctable.
failure_signatures: Options frameworks trained by the base option-critic objective alone run into degenerate solutions in the absence of proper regularization, where a sub-policy either terminates after each step (collapsing temporal abstraction entirely -- the option never demonstrates committed, extended behaviour) or runs for the entire episode regardless of state (never demonstrating state-sensitive, competitive selection) -- both are failures of exactly the middle-to-late rungs of ARC-130's ladder (competitive authority, committed throughput) despite the option's existence, representation, and local operability being intact.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Without an explicit deliberation-cost regularizer penalising the higher-level policy for switching options, option-critic architectures reliably learn degenerate solutions: either the termination function fires on almost every step (options collapse to primitive single-step actions, discarding temporal abstraction) or it almost never fires (one option runs for the whole episode, discarding state-sensitive selection). Adding a deliberation cost that explicitly prices option-switching restores meaningful, interpretable, temporally-extended options.
mapping.ree_translation: This is a clean, mechanistically-legible external instance of ARC-130's warning that stages of the causal-reach ladder are independent and a mechanism can pass an earlier stage (the option exists, is parameterised, and its policy executes -- existence, representation, local operation) while failing a later one (committed, state-sensitive, temporally-extended throughput) UNLESS something in the training objective specifically makes the later stage visible and rewarded. REE's own examples of authority-without-throughput (e.g. dACC strategy authority failing to reach LOFC execution gain, cited in ARC-130's own depends_on) are architecture-specific instances of the same general shape this paper documents in a much simpler, fully-controlled RL setting: local operability is not sufficient evidence of committed downstream behaviour, and the gap is not hypothetical -- it is the default failure mode absent a mechanism designed to close it.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The specific fix this paper proposes (an explicit deliberation-cost regularizer penalising option-switching) is not itself validated or proposed for REE -- ARC-130 explicitly declines to authorise building any new runtime object or telemetry schema from this intake pass, and this entry should not be read as recommending REE adopt a deliberation-cost-style regularizer. The evidentiary value here is purely in the documented FAILURE SHAPE (authority/selection without committed throughput being the default, not the exception, in a comparable staged architecture), not in the paper's proposed remedy.
mapping.source_context: Reinforcement learning benchmarks (four-rooms navigation, Arcade Learning Environment / Atari), discrete and continuous action spaces, single agent, option-critic architecture as the base case being regularized.

confidence_components.notes: Well-cited AAAI paper, direct empirical demonstration (not merely theoretical) of the degenerate-options failure mode in the exact architecture the companion 2017 entry establishes. Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the FAILURE SHAPE (selection/local operation without committed throughput as a default outcome, not an edge case) maps cleanly onto ARC-130's central warning; the specific mechanism (termination-function collapse under an unregularized policy-gradient objective) is RL-specific and has no literal REE equivalent.
